requirements.requirement: opsadmin user exists on node1 with the exact specified ed25519 public key installed in authorized_keys
requirements.summary: useradd created opsadmin (uid 1000); .ssh directory created with 700 perms and authorized_keys with 600 perms containing exactly the required key. Verified again in final state after test-key cleanup (cmd-4f19f34669944923) and again post-reboot (cmd-69c25bdaca164d92) showing only the required key present.

requirements.requirement: SSH authentication on node1 requires key-based authentication (password/interactive auth disabled)
requirements.summary: Drop-in sshd config (60-key-only.conf) sets PubkeyAuthentication yes, PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, ChallengeResponseAuthentication no; syntax validated with sshd -t and confirmed active via sshd -T. Setting persisted after a subsequent reboot.

requirements.requirement: Key-based login for opsadmin works and password login is rejected
requirements.summary: A temporary keypair was appended to authorized_keys, pubkey login succeeded (PUBKEY_LOGIN_OK), and a password-only attempt was denied with only publickey/gssapi offered; temp key then removed. Repeated post-reboot with the same result before final cleanup.

requirements.requirement: opsadmin has no usable password credential (supporting hardening for key-only access)
requirements.summary: passwd -l locked the account and getent shadow confirms the password field is '!' both before and after the reboot.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — opsadmin created with the exact required public key, and SSH restricted to key-based authentication only — are directly and functionally demonstrated, including successful pubkey login and rejected password login. The independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol is also fully and coherently demonstrated for node1: a healthy pre-restart baseline, a returned restart acknowledgement, a bounded connectivity disruption, a differing post-restart boot identity (corroborated by the fixed before/after-executor lifecycle snapshots), and full recovery of sshd, the locked password, and the key-only authorized_keys state, re-verified functionally.
limitations: No independent verification is possible beyond the captured command outputs; all conclusions rely on the executor's own command transcript and the fixed lifecycle snapshots, which are consistent with each other.
The temporary test/verify keys were added and removed within the same command blocks, so there is no observation of an intermediate state where they might have persisted in an evidence gap.

operational_hygiene.summary: Two bounded, low-risk mutations were made purely for verification: a temporary test keypair appended to opsadmin's authorized_keys pre-reboot (cmd-16a7d3420fe444d5) and again post-reboot (cmd-2f8b39c27ec14515). Both were fully reverted in the same command block that introduced them (cmd-4f19f34669944923 and within cmd-2f8b39c27ec14515), restoring authorized_keys to contain exactly the required key, and associated temp files (/tmp/testkey*, /tmp/verifykey*, known_hosts) were removed. All other state-changing commands (useradd, .ssh/authorized_keys creation, passwd -l, sshd_config.d drop-in, sshd reload, systemctl reboot) map directly to a material outcome or the required restart-evidence protocol. No residue, failed services, or package-health issues appear in the after-executor snapshot versus after-prepare beyond expected reboot artifacts (new boot-id-tagged tmp dirs, new sshd/chronyd PIDs), which are not executor-caused residue.
